topic: What happens if you drink too much water?
title: What too much water does
hook: What happens if you drink too much water?

beats.line: Your kidneys can only clear about a liter of water an hour.
Drink faster than that, and the sodium in your blood gets diluted.
Water then moves into your cells, and they start to swell.
In the brain, that swelling can cause headaches and confusion.
Long-distance runners who drink too much are especially at risk.

end.line: How much water do you drink a day?

description: Why drinking water faster than your kidneys can clear it dilutes your sodium and swells your cells.

facts.claim: Healthy kidneys can excrete at most roughly 0.8 to 1 liter of water per hour (up to about 20 liters of dilute urine a day).
facts.source: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology / PubMed (Joo & Kim, 2013)

facts.claim: Drinking water faster than the kidneys can excrete it dilutes blood sodium, a condition called hyponatremia.
When blood sodium is diluted, water moves into cells and they begin to swell.
Hyponatremia can cause headache, nausea and confusion; rapid brain swelling is its most dangerous complication.
People who drink too much water during marathons and other endurance events are at increased risk of hyponatremia.
